questions.q: What is the default failure mode when several teams respond to the same incident without coordination?
options: Each team investigates independently, re-discovering the same symptoms from different angles instead of testing different hypotheses
Only one team is ever paged, so the other teams never find out an incident is happening
The incident resolves faster because more people are looking at it simultaneously
Status page updates automatically merge across teams into one accurate summary
questions.explain: Paging is usually service-scoped, so by default nothing connects the responses together — teams duplicate effort instead of dividing the investigation.

questions.q: What does "one incident channel, one bridge, one source of truth" mean in practice?
options: Every team keeps its own channel, and the IC checks each one in turn
The moment an incident is multi-team, everyone moves into a single shared chat channel and/or call where findings, hypotheses, and status all get posted
Only the Incident Commander is allowed to post in the incident channel
The status page becomes the only place responders are allowed to communicate
questions.explain: A single shared space — not separate per-team channels — is what lets every responding team see what's already been found or ruled out, instead of rediscovering it independently.

questions.q: What is a pinned "current hypothesis + what's been ruled out" note used for?
options: It's a formality required for compliance audits only
It replaces the need for a Scribe to keep a timeline
It stops one team from re-testing a theory that another team already disproved earlier in the incident
It is only written after the incident is fully resolved
questions.explain: Keeping the current hypothesis and what's already been ruled out visible to every responding team is the single highest-leverage habit for avoiding duplicated investigation.

questions.q: What is the IC's job regarding escalation, according to this lesson?
options: Page every adjacent team immediately, just in case they're needed
Wait for teams to volunteer themselves into the incident channel
Page exactly the teams the current hypothesis points to, and escalate further only as the hypothesis changes — not flood the channel with people who have nothing to contribute yet
Never escalate beyond the first team that was originally paged
questions.explain: Paging every adjacent team "just in case" adds noise instead of signal. The IC brings in exactly the teams the evidence currently points to.

questions.q: How does a genuine major incident touching a dozen teams typically scale beyond the basic single-channel model?
options: By splitting into a dozen separate incident channels, one per team
By removing the IC role entirely once enough teams are involved
By skipping the hypothesis board, since too many teams make it impractical to maintain

By adding sub-leads per workstream reporting into the IC, a continuous bridge call, and regular timeboxed status check-ins — while keeping the same core idea of one source of truth and explicit ownership
questions.explain: The mechanism doesn't change at scale — one source of truth, explicit ownership, controlled escalation — it just gains layers like sub-leads and timeboxed check-ins as more teams are involved.
